title: Microsoft Purview DLP: block Copilot web search when prompts contain sensitive data (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap details, policy control, PowerShell call and prompt-protection licensing are supported by Microsoft sources. The documented limits and the narrowly stated documentation gaps also check out.

claims.claim: The roadmap modification timestamp is 2026-08-20T22:38:45.
The roadmap describes a real-time control preventing sensitive data from being used for external web search.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data leakage and oversharing risks by preventing Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat from using sensitive data for external web search.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes mitigating data leakage and oversharing risk.
claims.quote: This real-time control helps organizations mitigate data leakage and oversharing risks

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; controls[0].governs; Risk assessment
claims.claim: A DLP rule can block external web search for Copilot and Copilot Chat prompts containing configured sensitive information types.
claims.quote: When a prompt contains sensitive information types (SITs)—such as credit card numbers, passport numbers, Social Security numbers, or custom SITs defined by your organization—these experiences automatically block the use of external web search as a grounding source for that prompt.

claims.claim: Administrators configure the Copilot location with Content contains > Sensitive information types and Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches.
claims.quote:
Add a rule with the **Content contains** > **Sensitive information types** condition and choose the SITs you want to detect.
6. In the same rule, set the action to **Prevent Copilot from processing content** > **Performing Web Searches**.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The control is admin-opt-in and requires an administrator to configure and turn on the DLP policy before it restricts web search.
claims.quote:
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding. Valid values are:
- $true: Web grounding is blocked.
- $False: Web grounding isn't blocked. This value is the default.

claims.claim: A separate price or meter for the Performing Web Searches action is not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: "Performing Web Searches" "pricing" "DLP"; "Purview" "DLP" "Copilot" "meter" "price". Read the Copilot DLP location and Purview service description, including its Copilot licensing table; no separate action price or meter was stated.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal path Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Locations > Microsoft Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Copilot Cowork > Prevent Copilot from processing content > Performing Web Searches reaches the action.
claims.quote:
Go to **Data Loss Prevention** > **Policies** and select **+ Create policy**.
3. Select the **Custom** template, then **Custom policy**.
6. In the same rule, set the action to **Prevent Copilot from processing content** > **Performing Web Searches**.

claims.claim: New-DlpComplianceRule -Name "<rule name>" -Policy "<policy name>" -ContentContainsSensitiveInformation @{Name="<SIT name>"} -RestrictWebGrounding $true creates a SIT-matching rule that blocks web grounding.
claims.quote:
The ContentContainsSensitiveInformation parameter specifies a condition for the rule that's based on a sensitive information type match in content.
The RestrictWebGrounding parameter specifies an action for the DLP rule that blocks web grounding.
- $true: Web grounding is blocked.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Prompt DLP evaluates only the text typed into the prompt itself.
claims.quote: DLP only checks the text you type into the prompt itself.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: DLP cannot scan the contents of files uploaded directly into prompts.
claims.quote: DLP can't scan the contents of files that you upload directly into prompts, so evaluation of the uploaded file for sensitive data doesn't occur.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: When the web-search rule matches, Copilot continues generating responses using permitted internal Microsoft 365 sources.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: Microsoft names built-in and custom sensitive information types on the location's documentation page.
claims.quote: When a prompt contains sensitive information types (SITs)—such as credit card numbers, passport numbers, Social Security numbers, or custom SITs defined by your organization

claims.claim: The Learn page includes Cowork alongside Copilot and Copilot Chat in this web-search protection.
claims.quote: Restrict Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, and Cowork from using external web search when prompts contain sensitive data.

claims.claim: The roadmap item names Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat, not Cowork.
claims.quote: preventing Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat from using sensitive data for external web search.

claims.claim: The Learn page pairs Performing Web Searches with the sensitive information types condition.
claims.quote: | **Content contains** > **Sensitive information types** | **Prevent Copilot and Cowork from processing content** > **Performing Web Searches** |

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label conditions use a different action to prevent processing labelled files and emails.
claims.quote: You can create a DLP policy to prevent these Copilot experiences from using files and emails that have sensitivity labels when generating responses.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Sensitive information type and sensitivity label conditions cannot coexist in one rule but may use separate rules in one policy.
claims.quote: You can't use both content contains sensitive info types and content contains sensitivity labels conditions in the same rule. You can create a rule for each condition in the same policy, but not in the same rule.
